relevance_note: Case report of one girl with three heterozygous NOD2 variants and overlapping Blau syndrome / NAID features: "The tests identified three heterozygous anomalies in NOD2 gene".
method_note: Hand extraction, JSON assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory; every span checked verbatim against the paper by script. Scope: the patient plus her two parents (sex not given; 'Both parents tested negatively for mutations in NOD2 gene.'), labelled 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2'; no variant or feature rows for the parents ('healthy unrelated parents' excludes nothing specific). Table 1 has a 'Patient' column (√ = present). The legend defines '–' as 'non-characteristic', which describes the disease columns, not absence in a person, so '–' in the Patient column (camptodactyly, vasculitis, lung, kidney, serositis, IBD on endoscopy, etc.) was treated as not reported. Variants are printed without 'c.' prefixes: '2798 + 158C > T' (also given as 'IVS8_+158'/'IVS8^+158'), '802C > T' (= 'P268S'), '3016_3017insC' (= 'Leu1007ProfsTer2', also '1007 fs'); recorded as printed in cdna_hgvs_as_stated. No transcript printed. Inheritance recorded 'de novo' for all three variants because the paper states 'Both parents tested negatively for mutations in NOD2 gene.' (rule 8 literal reading); the paper does not describe the method of parental testing. Variant type for 802C > T recorded 'missense' from 'proline to serine substitution'; the intronic variant's type left not reported (paper says only 'substitution' 'within the 8th intron'). Pathogenicity 'pathogenic' from the abstract's statement about this patient's three variants. Possible tension in the paper: 'severe symmetrical knee and ankle arthritis' alongside 'Tenosynovitis and synovitis were excluded.'; arthritis checklist item set observed from the arthritis statement, synovitis and tenosynovitis rows excluded. Chronic meningoencephalitis is hedged ('suggested the presence') and recorded observed with that qualifier. Visual impairment checklist item set observed from 'left eye amblyopia'. Normal findings recorded as excluded abnormalities per D-27 (normal echogenicity, no lymphocyte subpopulation disorders, normal early development); 'endoscopic examination ... revealed no abnormalities' is a whole-investigation normal finding, recorded as written and excludes nothing more specific. Age at diagnosis not stated as an age (only 'ultimate diagnosis was established no earlier than after 4 years'), so left not reported; an earlier diagnosis abroad was 'sporadic sarcoidosis'.
